bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42537851 (haproxy): Heap-buffer-overflow READ {*} found by fuzz target fuzz_cfg_parser [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42537851
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / reproduction_report.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source
bug_description.normalized: The staged witness is exactly 50 space bytes with no newline. The `fuzz_cfg_parser` harness passes that blob directly to HAProxy as `cfg->content` with `cfg->size = 50`. In `parse_cfg()`, the first line-read call invokes `fgets_from_mem(thisline + readbytes, linesize - readbytes, &cur_position, cfg->content + cfg->size)` with `linesize == 2048`, `readbytes == 0`, `cur_position == cfg->content`, and `end == cfg->content + 50`. Inside `fgets_from_mem()`, `size--` turns the caller's 2048-byte destination-buffer budget into a 2047-byte newline-search span. The vulnerable code then calls `memchr(*position, '\n', size)` without first applying the missing bound `if (size > end - *position) size = end - *position;`. Because only 50 bytes remain in the input blob and the witness contains no newline, `memchr` scans past `end` and AddressSanitizer reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 2047` at `src/tools.c:6684`.

source.code: while (fgets_from_mem(thisline + readbytes, linesize - readbytes, &cur_position, cfg->content + cfg->size)) {
source.description: First project-side statement that consumes the raw fuzz buffer by passing its start pointer, end pointer, and caller buffer length into `fgets_from_mem()`.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` has sha256 `4c38d6d8bd1c5a3061e0c20067679faa28868831d7b838800e3b64729af34354`, length 50, and consists entirely of byte `0x20` (`' '`). The harness wraps it as `struct cfgfile { .content = (const char *)data, .size = 50 }`, and this first `parse_cfg()` loop iteration passes `cur_position == cfg->content` and `cfg->content + cfg->size == cfg->content + 50` into `fgets_from_mem()`.

tainted_value_origin.code: size--; /* keep fgets behaviour, reads at most one less than size */
tainted_value_origin.description: This converts the caller's 2048-byte destination-buffer budget into the exact 2047-byte `memchr` span later used at the crash site.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: On the crashing call `size` arrives as `linesize - readbytes = 2048` from `parse_cfg()`. After this statement it becomes 2047, which matches the saved ASan report's `READ of size 2047`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. `fgets_from_mem()` uses the destination-buffer-derived `size` as the `memchr` search span without first clamping it to the remaining input extent `end - *position`. The patch fixes this exact obligation by inserting `if (size > end - *position) size = end - *position;` immediately before the call.
root_cause.note: On the reproduced path `size == 2047` while only `end - *position == 50` valid bytes remain in the fuzz input buffer.

sink.description: ASan crash site. The unchecked `memchr` searches 2047 bytes starting at the 50-byte fuzz input blob and overreads the heap allocation.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 2047` at this call and says the faulting address is immediately after the 50-byte region `[0x5060000000e0, 0x506000000112)`.

parser_admitted.description: The harness's only admission gate is `if (size < 50) return 0;`. The staged 50-byte witness passes that gate exactly and enters HAProxy as an in-memory `struct cfgfile`.

coarse_trace.summary: The libFuzzer harness admits the exact 50-byte witness because `size == 50`, wraps it as `struct cfgfile`, and calls `parse_cfg()`.
On the first parser iteration, `parse_cfg()` calls `fgets_from_mem()` with a 2048-byte caller buffer budget but only a 50-byte valid source range from `cfg->content` to `cfg->content + cfg->size`.
The helper decrements that budget to 2047, omits the later fix's `size <= end - *position` clamp, and `memchr()` overreads the 50-byte fuzz input while searching for a newline that is not present.

fine_trace.code: while (fgets_from_mem(thisline + readbytes, linesize - readbytes, &cur_position, cfg->content + cfg->size)) {
fine_trace.note: Source. On the first loop iteration `readbytes` is 0 and `linesize` is `LINESIZE == 2048`, so `parse_cfg()` passes `size == 2048`, `*position == cfg->content`, and `end == cfg->content + 50` into `fgets_from_mem()`. The staged witness is 50 space bytes, so the valid source range contains no newline.

The EOF guard is false on the crashing call because `*position` still points to the first byte of the 50-byte witness and `end` points one past its last byte. Control therefore reaches the size arithmetic and newline search.

fine_trace.code: size--; /* keep fgets behaviour, reads at most one less than size */
fine_trace.note: This converts the caller's 2048-byte destination-buffer budget into `size == 2047`, exactly the read size later reported by ASan. No code has yet reduced that span to the 50 bytes actually remaining between `*position` and `end`.

Root cause and sink. The vulnerable code uses `size == 2047` as the `memchr` span without the missing patch guard `if (size > end - *position) size = end - *position;`. Because only 50 valid bytes remain and the witness has no `\n`, `memchr` scans off the end of the input blob and ASan reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 2047` at this call.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_42537851 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which fed the staged 50-byte `poc` to `/out/fuzz_cfg_parser` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 2047` in `memchr` called from `fgets_from_mem()`.

format.name: 50-byte in-memory HAProxy config blob for `fuzz_cfg_parser`
format.contract: The verified trigger is limited to the exact staged 50-byte witness in `poc` with sha256 `4c38d6d8bd1c5a3061e0c20067679faa28868831d7b838800e3b64729af34354`: 50 consecutive `0x20` space bytes and no newline. The harness must keep passing it directly as `cfg->content` with `cfg->size == 50`, so `parse_cfg()` reaches the first `fgets_from_mem()` call with `size == 2048`, `*position == cfg->content`, and `end == cfg->content + 50`. Under those exact witness-grounded conditions the vulnerable `size--` makes the `memchr` span 2047 and, because the input contains no `\n`, the unchecked search overruns the 50-byte blob. This GT does not generalize beyond that exact staged witness and no-newline trigger shape.
